problems.title: Standard form of a monomial product
problems.question: Simplify $(-2m^2n^4/(3p^3q))^2(3p^2q^2/(mn^2))^3$.
problems.idea: Simplify the exact algebra and use the defining geometric conditions.
formulas: Raise each factor to its power, then subtract denominator exponents. The coefficients give $(4/9)\cdot27=12$.
steps: The net exponents are m:4−3=1, n:8−6=2, p:6−6=0, q:6−2=4. Thus the product is 12mn²q⁴. The original denominators require m, n, p, q≠0.

problems.title: Natural values of a rational expression
problems.question: Find all positive integers n for which $(2n^2-8n-7)/(n-4)$ is a positive integer.
problems.idea: Simplify the exact algebra and use the defining geometric conditions.
formulas: Polynomial division gives $2n-7/(n-4)$, with n≠4. Thus n−4 must divide 7.
steps: The possible differences are −7,−1,1,7, giving n=−3,3,5,11. Discard−3 since n is positive. The expression at 3,5,11 is 13,3,21, respectively, all positive.

problems.title: A trapezoid tangent to a circle
problems.question: A trapezoid is both cyclic and tangential, has perimeter 20 cm, and one base is four times the other. Find its bases.
problems.idea: Simplify the exact algebra and use the defining geometric conditions.
formulas: For a tangential quadrilateral, opposite-side sums are equal. Thus the base sum is half the perimeter:10.
steps: If the smaller base is t, the larger is 4t and 5t=10. These lengths do for m a cyclic tangential trapezoid: equal legs 5 give height 4.

problems.title: All integer solutions of a linear equation
problems.question: Solve 10x−14y=26 in integers.
problems.idea: Simplify the exact algebra and use the defining geometric conditions.
steps: Write x=4+7t. Substituting gives 20+35t−7y=13, so y=1+5t. Conversely every integer t gives a solution.

problems.title: Equal-distance points on parallelogram rays
problems.question: In parallelogram ABCD with acute A, H is on ray AB and K on ray CB, with CH=BC and AK=AB. Given HDC=30°, find AKD.
problems.idea: Simplify the exact algebra and use the defining geometric conditions.
formulas: Use the intersections H, K distinct from B. Write $A=(0,0),B=(l,0),D=(p,q)$, with p, q>0 and $s^2=p^2+q^2$. Then $C=(l+p,q)$.
steps: The equation CH=BC gives H=(l+2p,0), the other solution being B. Write K=(l+tp, tq) on line CB. AK²=l² gives t=0 or t=−2lp/s²; the nontrivial solution is beyond B on the required ray.

Now DH²=(l+p)²+q². Also DK²=s²+l²−2D·K; since D·K=lp+t s²=−lp, this gives DK²=s²+l²+2lp=DH². We already have AK=DC=l and AD=HC=s. Hence triangles AKD and CDH have equal corresponding sides. Their corresponding angles AKD and CDH are equal.
problems.note: Distinct named auxiliary points are understood to be different from B, which itself satisfies both distance equalities. Allowing B for one auxiliary point and the other intersection for the other would require additional cases.

problems.title: A rational equation with excluded roots
problems.question: Find a for which $(a+2)/(2x^2-8)+1/(2x-x^2)=0$ has no solution.
problems.idea: Simplify the exact algebra and use the defining geometric conditions.
formulas: The domain excludes x=−2,0,2. Combining fractions gives $(ax-4)/[2x(x-2)(x+2)]=0$.
steps: For a=0 the numerator is −4, so no root exists. For a≠0 the candidate is x=4/a. It is excluded exactly when 4/a=2 or −2, giving a=2 or −2. The candidate can never be 0.

problems.title: Exterior bisectors of a trapezoid
problems.question: Trapezoid ABCD has AD∥BC, AD=9, BC=4, AB=5, CD=6. Exterior bisectors at A, B meet at M; those at C, D meet at N. Find MN.
problems.idea: Simplify the exact algebra and use the defining geometric conditions.
formulas: Each intersection is equally distant from the parallel base lines, so both lie halfway between them. Use $A=(0,0),D=(9,0),B=(u,h),C=(u+4,h)$.
steps: The exterior bisector at A points along (u/5−1, h/5), the difference of the unit directions of AB and AD. At height h/2 this gives M=((u−5)/2, h/2).
At D the exterior bisector points along ((u−5)/6+1, h/6). At height h/2 it gives N=((u+19)/2, h/2). Subtract horizontal coordinates: MN=(u+19−u+5)/2.
